articles.title: Rays 3, Guardians 1: He put the Fastball in Fastball Freddy
articles.summary: Monday night was not fun. But there was no time to sulk for the Rays, as they were right back at it tonight for Game 2 of the ALCS. You lose, and you face th...
articles.body:
Monday night was not fun. But there was no time to sulk for the Rays, as they were right back at it tonight for Game 2 of the ALCS. You lose, and you face the prospect of not getting back to the Trop, You win, and it's a brand new series in Cleveland on Thursday.

Freddy Peralta was on the bump for the Rays. Chandler Simpson returned to the starting lineup despite a lefty on the mound, with Ryan Vilade going back to the bench. Hicks also slotted back in behind the plate, but hitting eighth. More on him later.

Plant City native Parker Messick, expected to be an AL Rookie of the Year finalist, got the start for the Guardians.

The Rays traded for Peralta to not just pitch in these games, but put them in position to win them. He lived up to his "Fastball Freddy" moniker, throwing his 4-seamer 72% of the time. He got 10 whiffs on the pitch, and 5 more from his breaking ball and offspeed. He kept the heater up and oftentimes in, keeping the Cleveland lineup uncomfortable.

It looked to be another tight game that would be decided by the bullpens late. Messick looked sharp and kept the Rays off balance, but a horrible error from Jose Ramirez in the fourth unraveled the rookie's first ALCS start. With runners on second and third and two outs, Ben Williamson hit a routine ground ball to the future Hall of Famer, but it went through his legs and into left field to give the Rays the lead.

Liam Hicks, the very next batter singled to center, driving home two more.

Tough end to the night for the local kid Messick, and I'd be nervous to see him again later in the series. Four years ago I watched him face off against DeLauter in a college game. It was opening night between Florida State and James Madison at Dick Howser Stadium, and it was clear then that they'd both be serious big league prospects. I just wish I had known that one day they would be two impact players standing in between the Rays and an American League pennant.

Cleveland's only run came in the seventh, when Chase DeLauter doubled off of Ian Seymour to make it 3-1. But Seymour got the next batter, Jo Adell, to strike out and strand two runners in scoring position.

Baker came in for the ninth, and picked up his fourth save of the postseason, a new franchise record. The man is addicted to shutting the door.

Now, the series heads to Cleveland for the next three games, which are all guaranteed to be played after a Rays win tonight. Game 3 is Thursday at 8:00, and while no starter has been announced, Nick Martinez has yet to be used in this series and started Game 3 of the ALDS.

I'm not here to point fingers, but a stadium at 80% capacity for the biggest game of the season is disappointing. I don't have the answers, but every remaining home game will either be an elimination game or a World Series game. Any below 40,000 would be disheartening.

articles.title: Epic’s new games launcher is ‘vibe coded’
articles.summary: Epic Games is announcing a big refresh of its PC games launcher today in preview, but the company notes that the refresh was “vibe coded.”
articles.body: Epic Games is announcing a big refresh of its PC games launcher today in preview, saying that the new version is “way faster” and now supports Linux. But the company, which has been publicly making a big push into AI-assisted development, also notes that the refresh was “vibe coded.” “Programming is hard,” Epic says in a blog post. “So, instead of doing that, we vibe coded a new Epic Games Launcher that’s way faster and more responsive than the current one, and has a new look.” On Monday, CEO Tim Sweeney announced that the company has a “huge pivot underway,” where it will be “moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration.” Sweeney said the aim “isn’t to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal.” Bloomberg also reported this week that an Epic director on an unannounced Disney title told staffers that there would be “No more hand-written code.” “We used AI as a tool for this,” Martin Keely, Epic’s VP and GM of the Epic Games Store and Epic Online Services, tells The Verge in a briefing about the launcher. “It’s part of our migration as a company to use AI in new and different ways.” Keely says that AI has been “super helpful” for testing and for “replicating the core functionality from the existing launcher,” and he also notes that it’s also allowing Epic to offer the new launcher on Linux. [Image: Stats from Epic about the updated launcher’s speed. Epic has been working on the launcher for “most of this year,” Keely says, and while AI has helped Epic “accelerate our development,” the team working on the new launcher hasn’t adopted the “no more hand-written code” model reported on by Bloomberg. “We definitely had agents write and review all of the code,” Keeley says. “We used it to replicate the core functionality.” But the development team “managed that process” and “supervised the entirety of what we did.” Still, while the launcher team’s approach predates what Sweeney announced this week, “it’s on the same train,” Keely says. “The launcher is something that is demonstrative of the speed and efficiency both from the development process and the actual output that we think gives us confidence that the direction that we’re headed in is a positive one for our company and for gaming development overall.” The new Epic Games Launcher preview will be available on Windows, Mac, and Linux beginning today, and the old version will remain available. (Alongside the Linux version of the launcher, Epic is also announcing that it plans to bring Fortnite to Linux through the app.) Epic doesn’t have a specific timeline for when everyone will have to move over to the new version, Keely says, but the company will do the full launch when the update feels “stable” and has parity in “all places that we need” with the current launcher. In March, Epic laid off more than 1,000 staffers. “Since it’s a thing now, I should note that the layoffs aren’t related to AI,” Sweeney said in a memo to staff at the time. “To the extent it improves productivity, we want to have as many awesome developers developing great content and tech as we can.”

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto IV – The Legacy Review - IGN
articles.summary:
Grand Theft Auto IV legacy review by Luke Reilly. Reviewed on Xbox 360.
"Sentimentally speaking, Grand Theft Auto IV isn’t my favourite of the series – but I would say it’s the one I respect the most. It was bold to dial things back from the unhinged freedom of San Andreas in favour of a slower paced and more grounded crime saga, but it was a decision that allowed Rockstar to establish the importance of having a city so detailed it became a character itself, as well as flex a tech solution for character animation that has gone on to be a defining pillar of the series’ brand of emergent, slapstick fun. Obsessively detailed and impressively timeless, GTA IV is the prototype for modern Grand Theft Auto."

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Preorders Are $10 Off at Amazon and Walmart
articles.summary: Preorder your physical copy of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 at Amazon or Walmart to save $10 and secure the limited edition foil cover art as well.
articles.body:
In case you missed the memo, physical copies of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time are currently discounted at the likes of Amazon and Walmart. There's a $10 discount at both major retailers in the US, bringing the game down to $59.88 instead of $69.99.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2)

Preorders for Ocarina of Time have been live for a little over a month, and there's a jolly good reason everyone is so excited about it. It looks stunning, and we're now closer than ever to getting our hands on it.

But what's the deal with the immediate $10 discount at retailers like Amazon and Walmart? Well, it's actually fairly simple. As is Nintendo's custom for this console generation , the MSRP for the game is $59.99 for digital copies and $69.99 for physical copies.

But to encourage fans to buy physical games via their online storefronts, Amazon and Walmart have been fairly consistent at knocking prices down to match or even beat the digital price.

That's consistent for other Switch 2 exclusives such as Star Fox , Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave , and Switch Sports Resort , to name a few. But it's important to note that once the game is released, the price goes back up. So this is purely an incentive to preorder games.

So that's the deal! Plus, there's an even better reason to own The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as a physical copy as well. Nintendo also announced that the first printing of physical copies of the game would include "textured foil cover art" ... but only available while supplies last!

Plus, for what it's worth, for physical copies, the complete full game comes on the cartridge . No game key card.

Therefore, if you're down for a shiny textured foil cover for the game, which is limited edition, then your best bet is to preorder with Amazon or Walmart, and lock down your copy ASAP.

Plus, as a reminder, Amazon's preorder price guarantee means you don't have to pay for the game until it ships, and if there are any further price drops, you'll pay the lowest price possible (even if it goes back up in price before release day on November 5, 2026).

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches for Switch 2, November 5, 2026. It'll have more than redone load screens when it arrives, with players also still coming to grips with the wild changes Nintendo made to the game's visuals .

For more of what we saw during The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, you can read about the Link & Epona Lego set and the special edition console . For everything else revealed, click here .

For more on Ocarina of Time, check out IGN's preview of the remake - alongside this brand new feature where we discuss 29 new changes that are present in the new Switch 2 version of the game, including redesigned puzzles, updated miniboss fights, deeper dialogue, and more.

If you've been after the Z elda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 as well, it might be worth checking out Amazon, as the console has been going in and out of stock all week. Add it to your wishlist, and keep an eye on it throughout the day, and you should be able to secure it before October 29.

articles.title: Netflix Lays Off Over 1,000 People, Around 6% of the Workforce
articles.summary: Netflix has laid off over 1,000 staff in its biggest cutbacks to date, amounting to around 6% of its workforce. The cuts will predominantly affect its product, technology, legal and HR teams.
articles.body:
Netflix has laid off over 1,000 staff in its biggest cutbacks to date, amounting to around 6% of its workforce. The cuts will predominantly affect its product, technology, legal and HR teams.

“Our mission — to entertain the world — is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources,” co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters wrote in an email to employees, via WSJ .

“Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full-year forecast. We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high-impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation. Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors.”

Despite having a range of beloved exclusives, Netflix has struggled to keep up with audience demand lately, with some accusing it of adopting a quantity over quality approach. In a recently announced deal with Disney, Netflix plans to license shows from the rival streaming service to help meet demand.

In the deal, Netflix will host select Disney+ content for its 325 million subscribers, including a mix of legacy titles and currently streaming TV shows. Netflix recently announced its streaming lineup for October , which includes miniseries East of Eden, Ben Affleck’s Animals, and Josh Hartnett squaring off against a sea beast in Below. On October 20, Netflix will release the second season of its Studio Trigger-produced anime series, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 .

Netflix has also attempted to break into gaming to increase dwell time on its service. Most famously, the GTA 6 Extended Look was a Netflix exclusive for the first few hours. By all accounts, it was a hit, breaking 31.1 million views in its first week.

In June, the company released FIFA World Cup: Launch Edition as the latest game to include in its tucked away gaming section. But in August, the developer behind Netflix’s soccer game laid off 85% of its staff . Reviewers criticized the game's controls, graphics, AI, and pretty much everything else. In March this year, Netflix increased its prices again . According to Variety , a Netflix spokesperson said the company did not have any comment beyond the memo about layoffs.

articles.title: ‘We Vibe Coded a New Epic Games Launcher’ – Epic’s New Store App Was Built Using AI
articles.summary: Following reports of an AI push, Epic Games has revealed that the new EGS Launcher was "vibe coded" using artificial intelligence.
articles.body:
Epic has revealed a newly refreshed version of the Epic Games Launcher , its Steam-like platform that provides access to the Epic Games Store, your games library, social features, and a developer’s hub. In keeping with the company’s interest in and push for AI-assisted development , this new version of the launcher has been created using generative artificial intelligence.

“Programming is hard,” wrote Epic in a new blog post . “So, instead of doing that, we vibe coded a new Epic Games Launcher that’s way faster and more responsive than the current one, and has a new look.”

The term “vibe coding” is often used in a joke context to describe code developed entirely through AI prompts, rather than actual coding expertise. It’s interesting, then, to see Epic use the term in an announcement for its own product. But just how has the company approached the build of its new app?

During an interview with IGN, vice president and general manager of Epic Games Store Martin Keely discussed how the technology has been used. “We have used AI as a tool as part of our development process,” he said. “It's obviously an issue that's of high visibility at the moment across the industry, but for us, it made us more efficient and allowed a small team to rewrite the code base and be able to launch it faster across platforms, support Windows and Mac, and we're going to have a Linux version as well.”

Bloomberg’s recent report claims that developers at Epic have been encouraged to use Anthropic’s AI assistant, Claude, and that work on an upcoming Star Wars/Marvel crossover project should be conducted with "no more hand-written code.” Meanwhile, Epic’s founder and CEO, Tim Sweeney, said on X/Twitter that the company is "moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration."

When asked to clarify the extent of Epic’s use of artificial intelligence on the new launcher, Keely said that “it's been focused on code efficiency and the architecture, and allowing us to basically build features more quickly. It hasn't been about the artwork or the design style. There are some updates and changes, but that's been managed by our normal Epic Games design group.”

It’s interesting that this line has been drawn for the launcher, as Epic has been pretty open about how it’s used generative AI to help create Fortnite skins . The studio’s in-development Star Wars and Marvel crossover shooter is also reported to be using AI for its artistic assets, with Bloomberg’s report noting that all art for the project would be "generated with full AI workflows."

We’ve known about Epic’s plans for a new launcher for a while – we previously spoke to Keely’s predecessor, Steve Allison, who said that the app “should feel fast and snappy and just be what you expect, frankly” in our extensive interview . Of course, Epic also faces a cultural battle, as most PC players have been embedded in Valve’s Steam ecosystem for decades, with some convinced that the Epic Games Store will never be as good as Steam.

Matt Purslow is IGN's Executive Editor of Features.

articles.title: Ocarina of Time Remake Will Support All Existing Zelda Amiibo With In-Game Item Bonuses
articles.summary: The new Ocarina of Time Remake overview trailer has confirmed support for all Zelda amiibo, old and new.
articles.body:
Nintendo just dropped a new overview trailer for the Ocarina of Time remake, offering a fresh look at revamped environments, characters, and combat. We had the chance to play some of the game ourselves , and were surprised by just how many changes Nintendo is making to the iconic N64 release.

While Nintendo previously announced two new amiibo figures tied to the remake - Young Link and Young Zelda - the new overview trailer also confirms support for all existing Zelda amiibo. It doesn’t go into too much detail about what that support will involve, but the trailer shows Link receiving a number of helpful items, including healing hearts, Green Potions, and a Deku Stick.

It appears players can tap existing Zelda amiibo for helpful consumables and items, but not necessarily any exclusive cosmetics or weapons. This is similar to how non-Zelda amiibo worked in Tears of the Kingdom , which allowed for daily “bonus” scans of general Amiibo once per day.

The previously announced Ocarina of Time amiibo, which are up for preorder with varying levels of stock across retailers, will net players wearable masks for Zelda and Link.

Young Link amiibo - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

Young Zelda amiibo - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

Nintendo first launched the amiibo product line with the Wii U. Each amiibo comes with a small figure as well as a card that you can scan from Nintendo consoles, netting players various unlocks and bonuses across games.

Every mainline Zelda release has been accompanied by new amiibo. Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom Amiibo offered in-game weapons and gear in addition to daily rewards.

Amiibo frequently sell out in the lead-up to big game releases, and Zelda is about as big as it gets. While the Switch 2 generation of amiibo continues to be in stock at most retailers, some of the older releases have pretty much disappeared from the internet.

For those who are desperate to get their hands on an older release, GameStop offers tons of pre-owned amiibo with a solid ‘Pre-Owned’ guarantee for peace of mind. You’ll also find third-party resellers at Target, Best Buy, and eBay, though it’s always worth comparing prices to a figure’s MSRP at release.

articles.title: David Corenswet Reveals How His New Character is a ‘Superman-like Figure’
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview, David Corenswet and Isabel May discuss the heartbreak and hope of Mr. Irrelevant, and why the true story of John Tuggle rivals the Man of Steel's optimism.
articles.body:
David Corenswet’s turn as the Man of Steel in 2025’s Superman was awash in optimism, confidence, and swagger , and his next big screen appearance looks to be no different. In an exclusive interview with IGN, Corenswet reveals that the protagonist of his new movie Mr. Irrelevant, which hits theaters this December, shares a lot in common with the Big Blue Boy Scout.

“John Tuggle is a very Superman-like figure in a lot of ways,” Corenswet says. “I want to watch films that leave me feeling hopeful, optimistic, energetic. When the lights come up in the movie theater, I want to look to the people next to me and say, ‘Wow, we should be a little nicer to each other. We just went through something that brought us together, and I want to leave the theater and call my mom.’”

Mr. Irrelevant tells the true story of John Tuggle, “the last player selected in the last round of the 1983 NFL draft.” The movie stars Corenswet as Tuggle with supporting performances by Michael Shannon (Knives Out, Man of Steel) as legendary football coach Bill Parcells and Isabel May (Scream 7) as Tuggle’s love interest Katie.

Along with Corenswet, I sat down with May, who says playing Katie was a bit of a reprieve from some of her other upcoming roles.

“Of course I want to be a part of films that make people feel good,” May says. “But I also did films after this film that will make people not feel good.”

“I haven't made another film except for a Superman film since this film,” Corenswet adds. “Isabel has made quite a few films and it stretches the gamut. It's a wide range of characters and types of feelings that people are going to walk away from.

“[In one upcoming film] I play a pretty deplorable person,” May says. “But I want to play everyone, every kind of flavor of a person. I'm genuinely so happy to be here and talk about this movie because I'm so proud of it.”

How David Corenswet Prepared to Play John Tuggle

The real Tuggle died of cancer in 1986, and Mr. Irrelevant dives into the story of his health struggles and treatments in addition to his efforts to become successful in the NFL. Corenswet, whose own father died of cancer, says the former storyline was a more difficult and personal challenge for him to navigate as an actor.

“The second half [of the movie] was harder for me because that was all me. The first half is all my football double Jacob who gave and took all of the very hard hits over and over and over. I did a few of [the tackles], but we all knew that once I got worn out that Jacob was going to be the one to see it through to the finish line. [With the cancer scenes], the challenge is small things that you take for granted when you're watching a movie. If you're doing a scene where you're coughing, the scene might be 30 seconds or a minute on screen, but you spend all day coughing as an actor.

“In the same vein, this is the kind of movie where you almost hope that you'll end up with a scar or an injury so that you remember how much everybody gave to it. There's a lot of hard work that went into it all, but I was excited to go to work every single goddamn day on this film.”

David Corenswet and Isabel May Break Down Mr. Irrelevant's Shower Scene

While both Corenswet and May say portraying John’s health struggles was difficult at times, there’s one more lighthearted scene that was the trickiest for them to nail.

“There's only one that I remember,” May says.

“I'm wondering if we're thinking of the same one,” Corenswet adds.

“We probably are,” May says. “There's a scene where I'm taking a shower and David was having a really justifiably difficult time trying to figure out how not to be creepy and go in and someone's showering and bother them and make it feel romantic. But also still, if he didn't go in the shower, it wasn't as fun. So we were trying to figure out how to make that work.”

“That's the story I tell when I try to explain to people how good you were to have on set,” Corenswet says. “We had discussions about blocking but once we were up, we were trying to problem solve. [Director] Jonathan [Levine] said to me, ‘Is this the scene where it's all going to fall apart and we're not going to make the movie because you can't figure out how to walk in and not go over to the shower, but you have to go over to the shower?’

“We essentially got to the point where Jonathan and I said to each other, ‘We don't know how to do this.’ Isabel just piped in from the shower, ‘What if I don't open the curtain?’ And that immediately solved everything.”

While neither May nor Corenswet spoke with John Tuggle’s family while making the movie, they reveal that both Katie (to whom Tuggle would become engaged before his death) and people close to Tuggle have seen the film.

How John Tuggle's Family Reacted to Mr. Irrelevant

“I didn't get to meet Katie,” May says. “All I know is that she really, really loved him. She never remarried and that she stayed close to this family and was willing to have these conversations with people all these years later about this guy and was very supportive of us making this movie. Our producers showed the film to his sister and his family and to Katie, and they all said it felt like they were actually watching John. They got to see him again. So David tapped into something extraordinary.”

“[Katie] said that it was absolutely in the spirit of John and in the spirit of what happened,” Corenswet says. “And for a movie like this about a man who is not a household name, the point is that the spirit of it is true. This was a guy who made everybody else around him feel that there was more to be done and that there was a reason to smile and a reason to laugh, a reason to hope, a reason to get back up and keep fighting.”

As to whether the movie will bring more attention to John Tuggle’s life and on-field accomplishments, Corenswet says that he hopes it does more than that.

“We can all get on board with a Mr. Irrelevant movie about [someone like San Francisco 49ers quarterback] Brock Purdy,” Corenswet says. “About the guy who's picked last, who ended up being the star, the winner, the unlikely hero, the one whose name everybody knows and the story everybody knows. There’s an element to that when John starts his story. But what he learns and what most of us learn, and probably even the people who end up in the record books learn, is that the greatest impact an individual has on the world is not in the record books and it's not on the trophies in the glass cases. It’s on the people who you interact with and inspire.”

Mr. Irrelevant premieres in theaters December 25.

articles.title: Slow Horses Season 6, Episode 5 Review: River and Sid Shippers Get the Payoff They've Been Waiting For
articles.summary: “Sayonara” pulls out all the stops: major deaths, twists, big reveals, grand romantic gestures, and ridiculously huge explosions. It’s the most uncharacteristically Bond-like Slow Horses has been, and yet pulls it off in service of wrapping up Season 6 on a high note.
articles.body:
This review contains full spoilers for Slow Horses Season 6, Episode 5, which is streaming on Apple TV now.

“Sayonara,” the penultimate episode of Slow Horses Season 6, is just about as close to cinema as a single episode of TV can get… for better and worse. Set largely in foggy countrysides, the wide shots are hauntingly beautiful. It’s got big deaths (bye Jim, drowned in a lake) and twists (Jane survives the car crash!), high-stakes political drama (Diana Taverner’s heated committee hearing), classic spycraft (Jackson Lamb vs. Damien Cantor’s Russian contact), and tender moments between its characters (Sid Baker and River Cartwright, Catherine Standish and Reece Nesmith). Heck, it even ends with a grand gesture and huge car explosion. Slow Horses finally gets its Bond moment.

Oddly, it’s also sort of the antithesis to the series itself; since when do the Slow Horses get to have nice things? River (Jack Lowden) makes awful, nonsensical, emotionally driven decisions that seem to pan out mostly fine. The Horses posted up in Taverner’s country home are gorging on cookies and wine. River and Sid get to kiss, for chrissake! Those fleeting moments, however, are actually a bitter reminder that, no, it usually doesn’t turn out so well for the Slow Horses, as the season sprints to its finale that will, as Frank Harkness and his two minions promise, probably literally burn the house down. Diana Taverner’s holiday home, specifically.

Things pick up seconds after the last episode, where Sid Baker (Olivia Cooke) was kidnapped at gunpoint by confirmed GRU agents Jim (Kyle Soller) and Jane (MyAnna Buring), only now we’re seeing things from River’s perspective as he runs after their car. This really is Sid and River’s Big Episode; Sid uses the “River” novelty plate she bought last episode to slash Jane while driving to save herself from getting killed, even if it did put them all in serious danger when the car does a few barrel rolls and settles upside down. River swoops in to save Sid from being drowned and together they kill Jim.

The pair have a few sweet moments together amid the chaos. River finally tells her about his grandpa’s death. They banter about the most romantic ways to die in a black site hangar. They hornily flirt with each other right before Sid is meant to take off on a Russian plane to Bulgaria — a neutral, untracked place where she’d definitely be killed. And there’s River’s big moment, spurred by the power of a woman being into him: He punches out a few Dogs, steals an airfield maintenance truck, and hands himself over to the cavalcade of black cars to keep Sid from getting caught and sacrificed as retribution for Taverner’s off-book hit in Kazan. Maybe in a different life they could have been together, but it almost definitely won’t be this one.

Speaking of Diana Taverner (Kristin Scott Thomas), the First Desk is imperiously unwavering under scrutiny. There’s Lamb’s (Gary Oldman) reproach, as he’s pieced together that Diana scrubbed the Slough House records because she did use the identity of Sid, dead on paper and expendable, to cover up the Kazan assassination. Next is MI5’s all-male oversight committee as she’s questioned about the details of the same hit. In fact, she uses each as opportunities to pontificate about how she has the situation under control and how slow-moving and underfunded the service is. She hasn’t cracked just yet — buttressed by arrogance or necessity, I wonder? — and I’ll be curious to see if she makes it out unscathed or goes the way of all her other predecessors in the finale.

Slow Horses Season 6, Episode 5 — Images

At her holiday home, the merry band of Slow Horses is having a grand old time watching TV, drinking, and prepping Molotov cocktails. Lamb has Roddy Ho (Christopher Chung) digging up dirt on Damien Cantor (Harry Lloyd), but it’s Standish (Saskia Reeves) who finally gets something to do that isn’t staring at wine bottles or being mommy to a gaggle of whiners. Funny enough, it comes at a dinner table moment with Reece (Lenny Rush). Both have been grieving the deaths of not-so-great men they nevertheless had complicated relationships with — Standish, her old boss Charles Partner, and Reece, his dad — and neither would like to talk about it. Yet both play their conversation in a way that feels like they’re getting even just a little solace in finding a tiny amount of common ground.

The biggest curtain pull of the episode is one that we’ve been waiting for an explanation on all season (besides “why erase the Slough House records?”): What the hell is Cantor up to? Though it’s still not 100% clear, we know that he’s been courting mysterious Russian contacts for a media distribution deal, allegedly the biggest in Russian history. (Would he be airing Russian propaganda on his network or making the propaganda for the Russian state-run TV? Maybe both?) But Lamb isn’t far behind. He knows Cantor hired Harkness (Hugo Weaving) to take out Andy Nesmith, and Cantor has a strange, regularly scheduled meeting at a children's ballet rehearsal (based on the info gleaned from Ho’s detective work). He tails Cantor’s contact at the theater and then a bookstore, but she loses Lamb — not something a normie could pull off. Now all that remains are the last few pieces of the puzzle left to place.

articles.title: Spawn Gets 7-Inch Warlock Diablo Immortal Deluxe Action Figure - Fall FanFest 2026
articles.summary: IGN Fan Fest is kicking off today, and as part of the celebration, we’re showing off a Spawn Warlock action figure that commemorates the anti-hero’s special collaboration with Diablo Immortal.
articles.body:
IGN Fan Fest is kicking off today, and as part of the celebration, we’re showing off a Spawn Warlock action figure that commemorates the anti-hero’s special collaboration with Diablo Immortal.

As revealed at Blizzcon 2026 , Diablo Immortal is currently in the midst of a crossover event with Spawn, which runs from September 29 to November 1. This month-long extravaganza features a slew of new Spawn-themed challenges, abilities, and of course, a Spawn-themed cosmetic set.

The Warlock class version of this skin set is coming to the real world in the form of a 7-inch deluxe action figure from McFarlane Toys. Designed with ultra articulation and up to 22 moving parts, this figure has a full range for making cool poses. It includes a wired fabric cape, the Hellspawn Subjugator Sacrificial Blade, Demon Skull, and four alternate hands.

This figure also comes with an Elite Points card, which can be redeemed on the McFarlane Rewards website to snag rewards and one-of-a-kind prototypes, as well as a collectible art card.

Perhaps the most standout feature of this figure is Spawn’s wired cape, which manages to bring McFarlane’s signature, larger-than-life style to reality. The devil is in the details here (no pun intended), with every bit of in-game armor represented in the figure’s model.

Pre-orders are available now at McFarlane Toys’ official website and select retailers for $49.99. The figure is set to release in March 2027.

Diablo is having a big moment right now; on top of Immortal’s Spawn collaboration, Diablo V was announced at this year’s Blizzcon, which is scheduled for release in 2029. An animated show is also in the works at Netflix, though not much is known about the project at present.

We got the chance to interview the developers behind Diablo V to talk about the game, who confirmed that development is already in full swing. You can check out our conversation here , where they told us why this upcoming game is set 100 years in the future after Diablo IV and why they decided to announce the project so early.

articles.title: Honey, Xbox shrunk its controller
articles.summary: Microsoft is releasing an Xbox Nano controller. It’s a smaller and cheaper controller designed for gaming on the go.
articles.body: Microsoft is officially announcing its Xbox Nano controller today, a smaller and cheaper controller that’s designed to fit into your pocket. The more compact controller is also designed for “younger players, smaller hands, or anyone seeking something portable for play on the go.” The $49.99 Xbox Nano is Microsoft’s smallest controller, and it’s shorter than most smartphones at just over five inches in length. It has all the regular buttons you’d find on a normal Xbox controller, as well as Xbox Wireless and Bluetooth support for connecting to Xbox consoles and phones, tablets, and PCs. [Image: The Xbox Nano is designed for smaller hands and to fit into pockets. [Image: The Xbox Nano no longer has a tiny screen like leaked images showed earlier this year. The Xbox Nano controller also includes a rechargeable battery, and doesn’t require AA batteries or a separate charging pack like most Xbox controllers. Microsoft has also added a programmable Action Button to the Xbox Nano controller that can be customized to take screenshots, gameplay capture, and other Xbox shortcuts. The Xbox Nano originally leaked earlier this year with what looked like a tiny screen to indicate cloud or console connectivity. That screen isn’t part of this final shipping model, though. The rest of the controller looks identical to the leaks, including a USB-C port at the rear and a pairing button. The Xbox Nano is available to pre-order today, priced at $49.99. It will start shipping in November.

articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day Mod Adds Halo, Star Wars, and Warhammer 40,000 Skins
articles.summary: A Gears of War: E-Day mod lets players fancast your own team of Gears, with options from everything from Halo spartans to Space Marines from Warhammer 40,000.
articles.body:
A Gears of War: E-Day mod lets players fancast your own team of Gears, with options from everything from Halo spartans to Space Marines from Warhammer 40,000.

Incursion, from game designer Tom Whaley, aka @Unreal_Dev on X / Twitter , adds a skin selector to E-Day that lets you deck out Marcus, Dom, Mags, and Lucas in various skins. In addition to Halo and Warhammer options, there are Clone Troopers from Star Wars and even some in-universe appropriate Gears skins. You simply choose the skins from the new option in the main menu, or from the pause menu in-game.

What would #Halo made by The Coalition look like? — Tom Whaley (@Unreal_Dev) October 7, 2026

What would #Halo made by The Coalition look like?

The Incursion mod streamlines what’s usually a multi-mod setup for this kind of thing. Once you’ve got it installed, you can flip between skins at your leisure without needing to manually swap files or reinstall different character mods. While there are few limitations, you’ll of course need a copy of Gears of War: E-Day to run the Incursion mod pack. Check out the page on Nexus Mods for instructions on installation.

Last week, Alinea Analytics' head of marketing analysis, Rhys Elliott, reported that E-Day had sold an estimated 230,000 copies in its first week in what was described as a soft start. These unofficial figures, which are not backed by data provided by Microsoft, pointed to Xbox subscription service Game Pass as cannibalizing sales.

Earlier this month, the boss of The Coalition responded to reports that staff at the studio were worried they might lose their jobs amid the ongoing cuts at Xbox, promising the next Gears game wouldn’t take as long to make. Presumably future games will see the return of meat shields and chainsaw duels, features that were conspicuously missing from Gears of War: E-Day at launch. This is a direct consequence of the developers making the game from scratch, rather than using previous games in the series as a foundation.

For the uninitiated, Blue Eye Samurai is Netflix's gloriously bloody animated revenge drama set in 17th century Japan. It follows Mizu (voiced by Maya Erskine), a swordmaster whose distinctive blue eyes make her an outcast. Disguised as a man and armed with a frankly inspiring talent for slicing and dicing her foes, Mizu embarks on a quest to hunt down the four white men who were illegally living in Japan at the time of her birth in an attempt to find her father. The first season ended with Mizu setting sail for London to continue her search, and we'll get to see what she finds in the city in season 2. I think we can safely assume it's not all going to be cups of tea and crumpets.

Created by Michael Green (his other works includes Logan and Blade Runner 2049) and Amber Noizumi, the series debuted in November 2023 and went on to grab an Emmy for Outstanding Animated Program, which is a respectable achievement for a show featuring so many severed limbs.

Season 2 will arrive on Netflix in January 2027. A third and final season is planned for 2028, marking an end to Mizu's journey.

articles.title: Xbox Nano Controller Is Up for Preorder
articles.summary: Preorders are live for Microsoft's adorably tiny new Xbox Nano Controller.
articles.body:
If you could use a smaller Xbox controller for any reason, Microsoft has announced just the thing for you. It’s called the Xbox Nano Controller , and it’s a more compact, more rectangular take on the standard Xbox controller. All the regular Xbox buttons are accounted for, but the form factor is smaller and more portable. It’s a nice-looking device overall, and it’s available to preorder now from a number of retailers ( see it at Amazon ). It will release on November 4 for $49.99.

Regular, full-sized Xbox controllers are nearly perfect, in my opinion. But I’m a grown man with large hands, and I almost never have to bring my Xbox controllers anywhere. If your hands are smaller, or if you travel with a controller on the regular, you might want something designed just for you. That’s the Nano controller.

It’s just over five inches long and weighs a mere 3.5 ounces. Microsoft says it supports “all 18 standard gameplay inputs,” which sounds like a lot. It also includes a rechargeable battery and a programmable Action Button (that little Tic—Tac-shaped button in the middle) that Microsoft says, “can be customized for features like screenshots, gameplay capture, and other frequently used shortcuts.” Pretty handy.

And thanks to its Xbox Wireless and Bluetooth capabilities, it works with all the same devices as a regular Xbox controller, including Xbox, PC, Mac, and mobile devices.

Where the standard Xbox controller has grips that fit larger hands comfortably, the Nano has grips that slide into your pocket comfortably. But the design looks comfortable, and I like the white-and-black color scheme, complete with colorful ABXY face buttons. The sticks look a little shorter than on the standard controller, but the disc-style D-pad looks the same. I'd like to try this thing.

articles.title: Aaron Judge’s postseason absence adds a surprising twist to his Yankees criticism
articles.summary: Aaron Judge's criticism of the New York Yankees has taken an unexpected turn after injuries kept him out of the postseason. Following another disappointing p...
articles.body:
Aaron Judge watched from the New York Yankees' dugout as the Tampa Bay Rays celebrated their American League Division Series victory at Yankee Stadium. The Yankees had just suffered a 4-3 defeat in Game 3, completing a disappointing postseason sweep.

The Yankees captain responded by urging the organization to strengthen its roster and pursue another championship. However, his comments carried an unusual complication. Judge missed the entire postseason with a lingering right calf injury.

His absence has added another dimension to the criticism surrounding New York's latest October disappointment. While Judge wants the front office to make significant improvements, questions remain about his availability and the team's dependence on its biggest star.

Aaron Judge calls for major Yankees changes

Judge made his feelings clear after the Yankees were eliminated by Tampa Bay. The 34-year-old captain encouraged the organization to take an aggressive approach toward improving the roster rather than accepting another disappointing finish.

His message reflected growing frustration with the franchise's inability to turn regular-season success into championships. Despite consistently competing for playoff positions, New York has struggled to deliver the postseason results expected from its expensive roster.

Judge's comments also raised questions about accountability. While roster construction remains the front office's responsibility, his absence from the postseason has complicated the discussion about what prevented the Yankees from advancing.

His postseason absence changes the conversation

Judge did not appear in a single postseason game after suffering a right calf strain in September. The injury prevented him from participating in the Yankees' Wild Card Series victory over Boston and subsequent ALDS defeat.

General manager Brian Cashman explained that leaving Judge off the playoff roster was a medical necessity rather than a strategic preference. The slugger had not recovered sufficiently to handle running the bases or playing defense.

That distinction matters when assessing the criticism directed toward him. Judge wanted to contribute, but his physical condition prevented him from doing so. His absence was not a personal decision to avoid postseason competition.

Yankees struggled without their biggest offensive weapon

Judge appeared in only 66 regular-season games, batting .241 with 18 home runs and 41 RBIs. Injuries significantly reduced his availability, leaving New York without its most established offensive threat for extended stretches.

The Yankees still finished with 93 victories and advanced past the Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card Series. However, their offense struggled against Tampa Bay's pitching staff during the following round.

New York scored just 5 runs across 3 ALDS games and never held a lead during the series. The lack of consistent offensive production exposed how difficult postseason baseball becomes when scoring opportunities disappear.

Tampa Bay exposed problems beyond Judge's injury

The Rays defeated the Yankees in 3 consecutive games, ending New York's championship hopes earlier than expected. Tampa Bay combined effective pitching with aggressive baserunning and disciplined execution throughout the division series.

Defensive mistakes also contributed to the Yankees' elimination. New York committed 4 errors during Game 2, allowing Tampa Bay to capitalize on opportunities that become especially costly during short postseason series.

Those problems suggest that Judge's return alone might not have guaranteed a different outcome. The Yankees needed better defensive execution, timely hitting, and consistent performances across their roster to challenge a strong opponent.

Judge's leadership faces increased scrutiny

Judge has served as Yankees captain since 2022, carrying expectations that extend beyond his offensive production. His leadership role includes setting standards, supporting teammates, and helping maintain accountability throughout the organization.

Following the playoff elimination, some commentators questioned whether the team's clubhouse culture had become too comfortable. WFAN host Tommy Lugauer specifically criticized Judge's influence, arguing that the captain shared responsibility for the team's shortcomings.

However, criticism of clubhouse leadership remains an opinion rather than proof of organizational dysfunction. Judge's influence cannot be measured solely through postseason results, especially when injuries prevented him from participating in the team's elimination.

The Yankees' championship drought continues to grow

New York's latest elimination extended its World Series championship drought to 17 seasons. The franchise last won the title in 2009, when it defeated the Philadelphia Phillies to secure its 27th championship.

The drought has become increasingly frustrating because the Yankees continue investing heavily in competitive rosters. Their payroll approached $308.3 million, placing them among baseball's highest-spending organizations during the season.

Yet financial resources have not translated into another championship. The disconnect between spending and postseason success has intensified scrutiny of general manager Brian Cashman, manager Aaron Boone, and the organization's long-term direction.

Judge's injury history raises another concern

The judge's availability became a significant problem throughout the season. A fractured rib sidelined him for approximately 3 months before a separate calf injury prevented his return during the final weeks.

Those setbacks limited his opportunities to influence the Yankees' playoff positioning and postseason performance. They also highlighted the challenges of building an offense around a player whose injuries can significantly affect the lineup.

Judge remains capable of producing at an elite level when healthy. However, his age and recent injury setbacks make durability an important consideration as New York evaluates how to construct a more dependable championship contender.

New York faces difficult decisions before next season

The Yankees must now determine whether their current roster needs targeted improvements or more substantial changes. The judge's request for an aggressive offseason adds pressure on an organization already facing criticism from disappointed supporters.

Improving offensive depth could reduce the team's dependence on Judge while providing more flexibility during injuries. Strengthening defensive consistency and developing reliable postseason contributors should also be a priority in the organization's planning.

For Judge, the challenge extends beyond encouraging management to spend. Returning healthy, maintaining his offensive production, and helping establish a stronger team identity will be essential as the Yankees attempt another championship run.

Fun fact: The Yankees' 2026 ALDS sweep was only the second time they had been swept in a best-of-five postseason series. Their previous such elimination came against the Kansas City Royals in the 1980 American League Championship Series.

Aaron Judge urged the Yankees to pursue major roster improvements after their ALDS elimination against Tampa Bay.

A right calf injury prevented Judge from appearing in any postseason game.

New York lost all 3 ALDS games and scored only 5 runs against the Rays.

Judge's leadership, injury concerns, and the organization's roster decisions will face increased scrutiny heading into next season.

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners is back with a new season on Netflix on October 20, and today IGN's Fall Fan Fest featured a new teaser to remind you why you'll want to set aside some time for a serious Netflix binge as soon as it drops.

Season one focused on David Martinez, a student with a talent for tolerating cyberware enhancements and netrunner Lucyna "Lucy" Kushinada as they tried to survive Night City as part of its criminal underworld. Season two introduces a new story from the Edgerunners world with Roman Carax, a kid with a taste for old-fashioned movies, and Talia Yang, who is part of a cyberware partial criminal gang called Maelstrom.

After a special fan screening of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 at Anime Expo IGN got to put some questions to CD Projekt Red's Bartosz Sztybor the VP of Franchise and Saya Elder, Executive Producer - Anime about continuing the story after David and Lucy, how the New French Extremity style of horror influenced the games gorier scenes, and which character is the creator's love letter to cinema.

Was the success of season 1 encouraging or terrifying?

Bartosz Sztybo: Both. I’m a person that is never one hundred percent happy with what I wrote. So the success of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners was on one hand encouraging — that the stories I write can resonate with so many people. But on the other hand: “Oh, shit. I will never write anything that good again.” It was similar on other levels. From CD PROJEKT RED’s perspective and for Cyberpunk 2077 as an IP, it gave us a lot of confidence that people want such things and we have the strength to do them. But also — how do we top that?!

Saya Elder: It certainly gave us motivation! And confidence to fight for more anime projects.

With David gone, what was the biggest challenge in writing a completely new crew of mercenaries for an audience that got so attached to the first?

Bartosz Sztybo: The biggest challenge was to stop thinking about David and Lucy, and not get into a trap of artificially repeating things that fans fell in love with — or trying to create something extremely opposite. Of course, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 touches on similar things. It also rhymes with Edgerunners; there’s a dialogue between those two, but only to stay true to core principles of the Edgerunners franchise. The good thing was that I already had a few ideas while writing Edgerunners, so I just had to split my writing brain in two — one half to analyze Edgerunners and be able to stay true to it with Edgerunners 2, and the other half to keep unbiased, get back to the old ideas, and have new ones that will be something fresh.

Were there any areas you knew, sitting down to plan season 2, that you had to explore in the Cyberpunk 2077 world and hadn't had the chance too with season 1?

Bartosz Sztybo: I rarely think about the locations when I write or plan stories. I mostly think about themes and characters, so “unexplored areas” for me were not buildings, streets, or districts, but braindances and people working in that industry, backstories and private lives of corporate workers or again the edgerunners lifestyle but from a different perspective. Sometimes I have glimpses of scenes when I start thinking about the story and I search for visual metaphors when talking about or writing a scene, so then some places popped out, but I don’t want to spoil anything.

Incredible head pulping scene in that first episode. When it comes to gore, is there a something that let's you know you've nailed it when you see a scene, and have their been points when you've gone "ooooh too much"

Bartosz Sztybo: I’m a huge fan of David Cronenberg, Takashi Miike, and Julia Ducournau. I was super impressed in the early 2000s by the French new wave of horror, aka New French Extremity — Martyrs, Haute Tension, Trouble Every Day, À l'intérieur, and Frontier(s). Evil Dead is one of my favorite horror series of all time, so when you ask me about gore — I will always say more is better and I’m so happy that Kai Ikarashi digs that too. We understood each other perfectly, to sometimes go into exaggerated gore and sometimes show violence in a very cold, unemotional way with Cormac McCarthy and Michael Haneke as a reference. For real, in Edgerunners 2, you have never seen violence shown in such a way in the Cyberpunk 2077 universe!

Saya Elder: Gore and sex are areas where we typically give TRIGGER room to explore the scene organically during the storyboard phase. I've seen Sztybor try to convey the ideal level of violence in the scripts through onomatopoeia, like, “his head goes CRUSH” or "the building goes BOOM”, and maybe throwing out some wildly grotesque ideas for inspiration here or there. TRIGGER usually takes that and amplifies it in a way only they can.

Roman must be protected at all costs - how did his obsession with filmmaking shape the story of season 2?

Bartosz Sztybo — Everything was very organic. There was this old idea to include braindances in Edgerunners 2 and we started conversations with TRIGGER and Kai Ikarashi that led to certain narrative and visual choices. So Roman shaped Edgerunners 2, but also Edgerunners 2 created and shaped Roman. It’s inspired by the 90s when cinema was different than it is today, which led to an idea of a kid that thinks there’s value in the past, in a cinematic experience versus being plugged into a braindance. That led to many interesting visual ideas that you will see in the show.

Saya Elder: I actually fought so hard against having a child protagonist at first — I knew the audience would string us up by our thumbs the second anything happened to this baby! But Night City doesn't take it easy for anyone, not even a literal child. Roman is motivated by his desire to capture stories through his camera, and that motivation is the reason he keeps ending up in places where no child should ever be.

I loved the line about why stories matter, was that a theme you discovered early on? It feels very true to the CD Projekt Red ethos.

Bartosz Sztybo: Good stories are CD PROJEKT RED’s ethos, that’s true. And Roman is in a way a self-referential character — he’s my, Kai Ikarashi’s, and Masahiko Otsuka’s love letter to cinema. There’s also some of our experience there, when we dreamed about being filmmakers. And finally, it’s a metaphor for cinema's condition.

Saya Elder: Thank you! One of the themes we wanted to explore throughout the series was the generational loss of storytelling methods and technology. I remember talking to my younger cousins and realizing they had no idea what a VHS tape was. As someone who was raised on Disney and DreamWorks tapes, that was shocking and a little bit alarming. In the same way, old film and cinema represent a form of storytelling that is disappearing from Night City. We wanted to explore that in Edgerunners 2.

Speaking of themes, did the season's darker theme of revenge have any effect on the way you wanted the art style or animation to look to reflect it?

Bartosz Sztybo: The art style and animation are connected to a few things. They’re definitely linked with those 90s inspirations. But also some visual ideas, and the way violence is shown in some places, are sometimes meant to be uncomfortable. That’s not connected to revenge, rather to pivoting into a more realistic approach. And finally, Roman’s character gave us the opportunity to play with different points of views and different ways of visual storytelling.

Saya Elder: D is a character haunted by his past, and that surfaces through nightmare sequences and moments of trauma. TRIGGER portrays this in a very specific way. I won’t speak too much about the art style, since that’s TRIGGER’s domain, but one detail I love in Edgerunners 2 is how sweat is animated. It's very wet, and heavy, and unpleasant to look at. There's something deeply uncomfortable about watching characters break out in a cold seat.

articles.title: Invincible VS Players Can't Get Enough of Atom Eve's 'Thicc' Casual Skin
articles.summary: Atom Eve got a Casual costume in Invincible VS and, to no one’s surprise, the show’s fanbase is going feral for it.
articles.body:
Atom Eve got a Casual costume in Invincible VS and, to no one’s surprise, the show’s fanbase is going feral for it.

If you’re familiar with Invincible at all, you’ve probably seen some discourse online surrounding Atom Eve’s weight gain in the show and comics. We won’t spoil anything for you in this article, but it’s a byproduct of a major story beat in the source material, and her transformation is often looked on fondly by fans — if not outright preferred over her slimmer design.

The devs at Skybound Games have been hard at work developing new characters and costumes for Invincible VS , the show’s tie-in 3v3 tag fighting game, most recently unveiling Angstrom Levy as a playable character… but the big brainiac isn’t who’s got players talking right now.

Alongside this character, Skybound also released a few alternate costumes for its other characters, including a ‘casual’ outfit for Atom Eve. And while she’s certainly dressed down, it’s her weight gain that’s got the fanbase in a tizzy.

It’s safe to say that everyone’s pretty thirsty for this particular version of Eve, with one excited player writing , “We ALL copping Everyday Eve, right?”

“Invincible better be able to fight,” another joked .

“The people yearn for thicc Eve,” yet another said .

A new Invincible VS Skin for every Casual Friday, Dressed Up Weekend, and Duct-Tape Wednesday. — Invincible VS (@InvincibleVS) October 14, 2026

A new Invincible VS Skin for every Casual Friday, Dressed Up Weekend, and Duct-Tape Wednesday.

Still others are pleasantly surprised that the devs at Skybound chose to go in this direction for Eve’s alternate costumes, given that body diversity isn’t something seen very often for female characters in fighting games (though this is a trend that’s changing in more recent releases, with Marisa in Street Fighter 6 being a good example).

Invincible VS is leaning into the memes with its costumes and characters lately; Skybound also gave Mark a Duct-Tape Man costume (leaning into a ‘superhero costume’ he made in his childhood) and even including Agent Spider as a playable fighter, a character who’s basically a riff on Marvel’s Spider-Man, for all intents and purposes.

Invincible VS released earlier this year. IGN scored the game a seven out of 10 , with our reviewer Mitchell Saltzman saying its “hard hitting and fast paced 3v3 tag fighting is a gust of fresh air, especially for those who miss the two-way interactable combo system of Killer Instinct.”

The next season of Invincible is scheduled to release on Prime Video in early 2027. The show has been renewed for a sixth season, as well, becoming the platform’s longest-running animated series to date.

articles.title: GTA 6 Was Originally Meant to Release Much Sooner Than We Realized
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has revealed that it originally intended to develop GTA 6 alongside Red Dead Redemption 2, meaning it probably would've come out much sooner than we ever realized.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games has revealed that it originally intended to develop GTA 6 alongside Red Dead Redemption 2, meaning it probably would've come out much sooner than we ever realized.

As told in a new article from Bloomberg , Rockstar Games initially planned to develop Red Dead 2 and GTA 6 at the same time, but that quickly became infeasible. Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson recognized that the ambition behind Red Dead Redemption 2 meant they would need to treat it as an all-hands-on-deck situation, which also meant putting GTA 6 on the back burner. However, GTA 6 would benefit from this, as Nelson noted to Bloomberg that everything they built for Red Dead would "pay off" in GTA 6.

That appears to be true, as GTA 6 uses a lot of ideas and systems from Red Dead Redemption 2, including its NPC interaction system. It seems unlikely that GTA 6 would be what it is today if it had stayed the course and been developed in tandem with the western sequel. Unfortunately for fans, it means the game took much longer to make. Had it been developed simultaneously, it seems likely that Rockstar would've been able to release GTA 6 in the early 2020s.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

Of course, the first release window that Rockstar ever actually publicly provided for GTA 6 was 2025. The game was delayed a couple of times, much to the bewilderment of Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two Interactive. Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe noted that she had to call Zelnick just months after announcing the game's first delay to inform him that they would need more time.

“I think he said, ‘You’re kidding. Please tell me you’re kidding,’” recalled Kolbe to Bloomberg. “But once we talked through why, he got it. And I think we are really lucky that he is as reasonable as he is, because a lot of people would say, ‘You’d just better figure out how to ship it.’ And we have been really, really lucky that we have not found ourselves in that place, because that happens to a lot of teams, and we’ve all played those games. It’s not great.”

Bloomberg's report dispels rumors that GTA 6 has been in active development since shortly after GTA 5 was released in 2013, but that doesn't mean Rockstar only began working on it after Red Dead 2's launch. Various teams and leadership within Rockstar have been researching and planning GTA 6 since as early as 2014. Rockstar has spoken at length in recent interviews about taking staff to Florida to research and dream up ideas for GTA 6 during the mid to late 2010s.

Bloomberg noted that the team didn't have a "skeleton" for GTA 6's story until the end of 2019, a year after Red Dead 2's release. Even then, it took a while before the team was able to fully wrap its head around what the game would be. Rockstar has vowed to not take nearly as long on its next game , thanks to the fact it seems to have fewer obstacles going forward.

Rockstar doubled in size during GTA 6's development, encountered multiple leaks, had a loss in productivity during the pandemic, and much more. The studio also made major changes to how it operates and expects that will set it up for success moving forward. What is Rockstar's next game? We don't know. Some may expect Red Dead 3, but other fans are hoping that Rockstar will break the cycle of alternating between Red Dead and GTA in favor of something new or reviving a different IP. Whatever the case is, don't expect it to take another eight years.

articles.title: Jeremy Renner Is Teasing the West Coast Avengers in the MCU, and It's About Time
articles.summary: Jeremy Renner has teased the return of Hawkeye to the MCU in a West Coast Avengers project. Here's why we think that's an excellent idea.
articles.body:
When Jeremy Renner tweets, the Internet pays attention. Renner has now raised eyebrows with a post that seems to suggest he’s doing some reading in preparation for a new MCU project . We don’t know if it’s a series or a movie, but it appears to be an adaptation of the classic West Coast Avengers comic.

Who are the West Coast Avengers, and why might they be getting the MCU spotlight now? Let’s quickly break down what you need to know.

Marvel Cinematic Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

In this case, the name is pretty self-explanatory. The Avengers are traditionally located in New York, where they generally operate out of either the Avengers Mansion or Stark Tower (or both). The idea with West Coast Avengers was twofold - spotlight some of the heroes who weren’t getting their due in the main Avengers comic, and give the Marvel Universe’s version of America a superteam that wasn’t based in the same major metropolis.

The team officially made their debut in 1984’s The West Coast Avengers #1, created by Roger Stern and Bob Hall. The initial lineup included Hawkeye, Mockingbird, Iron Man (Rhodey, not Tony), Tigra, and Wonder Man. While the first series only spanned four issues, it was quickly followed by an ongoing series that lasted a full decade and brought in new members like Moon Knight, Tigra, U.S. Agent, Vision, and Scarlet Witch.

In the years since, Marvel has revived the West Coast Avengers a number of times with different lineups. They even went through a phase after 2006’s Civil War where Iron Man instituted the 50-State Initiative and gave every single US state its own team. Yes, even Iowa.

The original series has added a lot to the larger Avengers mythology, including elevating Hawkeye to team leader status. It’s also significant for delving deeper into the romance between Vision and Scarlet Witch and the creation and destruction of their magically generated children. You don’t get WandaVision and its spinoffs, or Paul Bettany’s White Vision, without first having West Coast Avengers.

Why the MCU Needs the West Coast Avengers

So why is Renner reading up on this classic Marvel team? It stands to reason that Marvel is looking to make a West Coast Avengers project a priority in the next phase of the MCU. And just as in the comics, it appears that Hawkeye will be a major force in spearheading the team.

Honestly, now is probably the right time to move forward with West Coast Avengers. We currently have two different Avengers teams in the MCU – the New Avengers are operating out of the old Stark Tower in New York, and Anthony Mackie’s Captain America is currently leading a small team, but there’s still the problem that the western half of the country is badly underprotected. Why should the East Coast get all the superheroes?

More importantly, West Coast Avengers is valuable in its ability to bring together a number of Disney+ MCU characters who are currently stuck in limbo. Marvel continues to drag its heels on greenlighting a second season of Hawkeye. Perhaps a West Coast Avengers series could be its replacement, bringing back not just Renner’s Clint Barton but also Hailee Steinfeld’s Kate Bishop? Both characters did headline the 2018 West Coast Avengers comic, after all.

There are plenty of other characters who would make sense as team members. What about Tatiana Maslany’s She-Hulk (easily the MCU’s most prominent California-based hero) or Oscar Isaac’s Moon Knight? Or how about Yahya Abdul-Mateen II’s Wonder Man? It still stings that Marvel opted to cancel Wonder Man Season 2 after the strong critical reception to Season 1 , but maybe they did so to make room for Simon Williams’ inclusion on an Avengers team instead? We can certainly hope.

Then there are Vision and Scarlet Witch. We don’t yet know where VisionQuest will leave Bettany’s character, nor whether those rumors about Elizabeth Olsen’s Wanda Maximoff getting resurrected will pan out. But assuming the two characters are kicking around after the events of Avengers: Secret Wars, it would make sense to include them and their now-adult children in West Coast Avengers as well.

Basically, West Coast Avengers can allow Marvel to finally dust off these underutilized characters and give them a new home with a more marketable brand. Ideally, the project would be a series rather than a movie, just based on the number of characters it would need to juggle. And, hey, MCU fans need something more than just Zodiac to look forward to on the live-action MCU series front.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: Andrew Schulz Explains His Viral Mortal Kombat Movie Callout at the Game Awards
articles.summary: Andrew Schulz explained the viral moment when he called out the cast of the Mortal Kombat II movie, saying he was hoping for a 'Barbenheimer' moment and a possible collaboration between the two fighting game franchises.
articles.body:
At the 2025 Game Awards, actor, comedian, and podcast host Andrew Schulz infamously called out the cast of the second Mortal Kombat movie while promoting the Street Fighter film, in which he stars as Dan Hibiki.

“We’re not the only game that appreciates your patronage,” Schulz said. "There's another game out there. They also flew from around the world to be here because they appreciate you. So give it up for the whole cast of Mortal Kombat 2 !”

It turns out that the cast hadn’t actually shown up for the Game Awards, which Schulz capitalized on for his bit on stage. “Just kidding,” he continued. “They didn’t come. They don’t care about you, they only care about money, okay? We care about money and you! Street Fighter forever!”

The cast of the Street Fighter Movie just threw BIG shots at the Mortal Kombat Movie Kast at #TheGameAwards! Oh it's on! 😤 — David | unCAGEDgamez (@unCAGEDgamez) December 12, 2025

The cast of the Street Fighter Movie just threw BIG shots at the Mortal Kombat Movie Kast at #TheGameAwards! Oh it's on! 😤

Although his fellow cast members clarified that he was merely joking, Schulz’s callout went viral, with many fans feeling like this was an unfriendly jab at a fellow fighting game adaptation. Even actor Lewis Tan, who starred in the films, spoke about the ordeal , saying Schulz was the "last person that should be talking shit on that stage."

I got the chance to ask Schulz about this joke ahead of the Street Fighter movie’s release — and Schulz told me that he was merely trying to stoke the flames of a good-natured rivalry with the Mortal Kombat II cast in classic pro wrestling fashion.

“Guys, I thought we were in this together! In the wrestling business, this is called a ‘work,’ right?” Schulz began.

“Yep. You were workin’, they were shootin’,” Cody Rhodes confirmed.

“I read what was on the prompter,” Schulz continued. “...I thought that we were gonna turn into Barbenheimer. You know, rising tides lift all boats.”

“But you dissed them,” Eric Andre interjected.

“I got them a lot buzz,” Schulz countered.

“Here’s a follow-up,” Rhodes said, looking at me. “Do you have a Mortal Kombat tattoo?”

(I feel the need to explain; you might’ve seen the viral clip of this trio asking me to show them my M. Bison tattoo during this same interview. If not, you can watch it down below.)

"Exactly,” Schulz said, to which Cody responded that he wasn’t “trying to fire another shot.”

“I was waiting for a thank you!” Schulz joked when I asked for his thoughts on the debate that his remarks had stirred up online. “You know, we used our platform to promote our movie to promote another movie! I feel like that's a very generous thing to do!”

Since we were on the topic of Mortal Kombat, I had to bring up the fact that the series’ co-creator, Ed Boon, recently expressed interest in a potential crossover game with Street Fighter. When asked if they’d be willing to star in a crossover film with the franchise, Schulz told me that was essentially what he was trying to accomplish with his viral callout at The Game Awards.

“This is what we were trying to do at [The Game Awards]!” Schulz said. “We’re trying to set this thing up!”

“That’s what we were trying to do,” Cody Rhodes added.

“Tell them I know Noob Saibot which is [Ed Boon's and John Tobias’] names backwards,” Eric Andre interjected. “...But a crossover? A Flinstones/Jetsons crossover? We’re in. Let’s go.”

(All three actors clarified that they have nothing but love for the Mortal Kombat franchise and the cast in the films; this hilarious trio was merely bantering with me about the situation, but it's clear they are definitely willing to work with the Mortal Kombat folks in some capacity.)

This was a sentiment echoed by most of the Street Fighter cast members that I interviewed. Almost every one of them were game for a possible collaboration with another fighting game franchise, with Andrew Koji and Callina Liang specifically mentioning Marvel vs Capcom .

However, director Kitao Sakurai has made it clear that any future Street Fighter films depend on how well the first one performs in theaters. Having seen it myself, I can say that it’s very good fun and full of lore and Easter eggs that fans will enjoy — but you’ll have to form your opinion when you sit down to watch it for yourself.

Street Fighter hits theaters on October 16, 2026.

articles.title: The Pokémon Center's New 'Winter Night Sky' Holiday Collection Comes With a Free Sticker Sheet
articles.body:
The Pokémon Center just dropped its 2026 holiday collection, revealing this year’s theme as ‘Winter Night Sky.’

Like any TPC merch drop, the full list of 60+ new products is all over the place. The designs are generally unified by starry skies and pastel auroras, with new illustrations of Pokémon getting up to some festive activities.

The collection, which includes a mix of decor, apparel, and gift-wrapping accessories, is now available exclusively from The Pokémon Center. Any purchases from the collection before December 25 will come with a free Winter Night Sky sticker sheet, while supplies last.

'Winter Night Sky' Holiday Collection Now Available at The Pokémon Center

The very literal star of the show is Mew, who made it to the big leagues as this year’s tree topper . The ethereal Pokémon is also getting a dedicated stocking, listed at $19.99 .

Of course, this wouldn’t be a holiday collection without some new Pokémon decorations for your tree. New individual ornaments feature detailed holiday-themed models of Slowpoke, Amaura, Piplup, and a spread of Eeveelutions. The retailer also has new themed packs of standard round baubles.

If you’d rather have your beloved Pokemon firmly planted on a surface, TPC dropped three new additions to its Holiday Village figure collection: Town Hall Greetings , Meloetta Majestic Theatre , and Yamper Snowy Scamper .

Together for the Holidays Ornaments (8-Pack)

Espeon Purple Knit Beanie (One Size-Adult)

Winter Night Sky Pokémon Holiday Puzzle (1,000 Pieces)

Festive Pikachu and Eevee Small Gift Box

On the apparel side, we’re seeing new sets of cozy pajamas as well as some t-shirts and knit beanies. Per Pokémon’s press release , “These cheerful cold-weather companions are ready to keep Trainers warm, cozy and full of wonder all winter long.”

There’s plenty more random things in the full collection. Again, the full list includes over 100 new products. A personal standout is the new 1,000-piece puzzle which features my beloved Piplup, but you’ll find everything from table runners and tea towels to snow globes and blankets.

I’m of the opinion that any of these would make great gifts. For what it’s worth, the collection also includes a ridiculous amount of gift boxes and bags that I would cherish just as much as whatever ends up being inside.
